sn.s: En Granada casi no hay taxis normales.
sn.e: In Granada there are hardly any normal taxis.
There are mototaxis.
A mototaxi has three wheels.

sn.s: Una rueda adelante y dos ruedas atrás.
sn.e: One wheel at the front and two at the back.
The mototaxi has no doors.
The engine is loud.

sn.s: El motor suena como una máquina de coser.
sn.e: The engine sounds like a sewing machine.

sn.s: Aquí al mototaxi le dicen caponera.
sn.e: Here they call the mototaxi a caponera.

sn.s: Caponera es la palabra de la gente.
sn.e: Caponera is the word people use.

sn.s: Mototaxi es la palabra del papel.
sn.e: Mototaxi is the word on paper.

sn.s: Roberto llama una caponera con la mano.
sn.e: Roberto waves a caponera down.

sn.s: La caponera para en la esquina.
sn.e: The caponera stops at the corner.
Roberto does not get in yet.
First he talks to the man.
"How much to the park?" he asks.
"Thirty," the man says.
"Thirty? It's close, man."
"All right, twenty-five."
"Dale," Roberto says.
And now we get in.
That is the agreement.

sn.s: El acuerdo se hace antes de subir.
sn.e: The agreement is made before getting in.
Never afterwards.

sn.s: Si uno sube sin acuerdo, paga lo que digan.
sn.e: If you get in without an agreement, you pay whatever they say.

sn.s: Y lo que digan va a ser más.
sn.e: And whatever they say is going to be more.
Roberto says it plainly.
"The agreement first. Always."
"Even if it is close. Even if it is short."
The journey is short.
It is only five blocks.

sn.s: Pero con este calor cinco cuadras es lejos.
sn.e: But in this heat five blocks is far.

sn.s: Adentro de la caponera corre el aire.
sn.e: Inside the caponera the air moves.

sn.s: Sin puertas, el aire entra por todos lados.
sn.e: With no doors, the air comes in from everywhere.

sn.s: Eso es lo bueno de no tener puertas.
sn.e: That is the good thing about having no doors.
We go fast between the cars.

sn.s: La caponera pasa por donde no cabe un carro.
sn.e: The caponera goes where a car does not fit.
I hold on tight.

sn.s: Roberto va tranquilo, como en su casa.
sn.e: Roberto sits calmly, as if at home.

sn.s: Llegamos al parque en tres minutos.
sn.e: We arrive at the park in three minutes.

sn.s: Le pago veinticinco pesos al señor.
sn.e: I pay the man twenty-five pesos.
Exactly what we said.
With no argument and no trouble.

sn.s: Al otro día tomo una caponera solo.
sn.e: The next day I take a caponera on my own.
"How much to the market?" I ask.
"Fifty," the man says.

sn.s: Yo sé que el mercado está cerca.
sn.e: I know the market is close.
"It's close. Thirty?" I say.

sn.s: El señor me mira un momento.
sn.e: The man looks at me for a moment.
"Thirty-five."
"Dale pues," I say.
And I get in.
Thirty-five, not fifty.
Fifteen pesos are nothing.

sn.s: Pero yo no pagué de chele.
sn.e: But I did not pay a chele's price.
I paid a local one.
